title: Investigating physical states of molecular gas in the overlapping region of interacting galaxies NGC 4567/4568 using ALMA
question: Do molecular clouds in the filament and overlapping region of the early-stage interacting pair NGC 4567/4568 show higher virial parameters and a higher CO(3-2)/CO(1-0) ratio (denser gas) than disc clouds, as simulations of collisional compression predict?

recipe.goal: calibrate and image the CO(1-0) and CO(3-2) cubes
recipe.method: Calibration and imaging in CASA; continuum undetected; continuum subtraction with uvcontsub; primary beam correction; tclean with Briggs weighting; 12-m and ACA combined

recipe.goal: make moment maps and measure integrated intensities and luminosity mass
recipe.method: Moment maps clipped at 3 sigma (CO 3-2 integrated intensity) and 5 sigma (velocity field and dispersion); luminosity mass from CO(1-0) flux with the Kenney and Young relation
key_parameters: clip level 5 sigma on CO(1-0) velocity field and dispersion maps (1 sigma = 1.5 mJy/beam)
assumptions: XCO = 2.0 x 10^20 cm^-2 (K km/s)^-1; distance 16 Mpc

recipe.goal: build position-velocity diagrams across the filament
recipe.method: P-V diagrams perpendicular to the filament from the CO(1-0) cube

recipe.goal: identify molecular clouds in the CO(1-0) cube and assign them to regions
recipe.method: CLUMPFIND in 3D with contour levels starting at 3 sigma and spaced by 2 sigma; separate noise levels for overlapping and disc regions; filament membership from position and P-V velocity criteria
key_parameters: cloud must exceed beam size (~100 pc) and the 5 km/s velocity resolution; clouds truncated at the field edge excluded
filament defined as integrated intensity > 0.5 Jy km/s in the white box and emission above 4.5 mJy/beam (3 sigma) in the P-V diagram

recipe.goal: derive cloud physical properties and virial parameters
recipe.method: Radius and velocity dispersion from CLUMPFIND after deconvolution; luminosity mass from CO(1-0) integrated intensity, projected area and XCO; surface density = mass / area for a spherical cloud; alpha_vir = 5 sigma^2 R / (G M_CO)
assumptions: cloud treated as a sphere for mass surface density; alpha_vir below about 1 means gravitationally bound

recipe.goal: compare cloud populations between disc and overlapping regions
recipe.method: Two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test on each cloud property at the 1% significance level

recipe.goal: measure CO(3-2)/CO(1-0) intensity ratio per cloud
recipe.method: R3-2/1-0 = I(CO 3-2)/I(CO 1-0) from pixel values inside the clouds identified in the CO(1-0) cube; clouds in the disc region not plotted

recipe.goal: test cluster stripping and compare CO with HI and H-alpha
recipe.method: Compare galaxy-scale HI and CO distributions; split NGC 4568 into northern and southern discs using an ellipse fit to the HI 3 sigma level; compare HI mass in the two halves; overlay R3-2/1-0 with H-alpha

recipe.goal: model the disc kinematics and look for departures from circular motion
recipe.method: 3D-BAROLO kinematic models assuming circular motion compared with the Cycle 1 CO(1-0) data of each galaxy

score_reason: ALMA project codes and the main analysis recipe (tclean Briggs 0.5, uvcontsub, CLUMPFIND 3 sigma/2 sigma, formulae) are given with numeric results, but CASA version, masks, cell sizes, beam sizes and several external datasets are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Project codes are given and the cloud identification and ratio analysis are simple and numeric, so a rough reproduction of cloud counts, virial parameters and R3-2/1-0 is plausible, although exact numbers need unstated settings.
